topIssues.title: Consensus-layer sync fails with pruned history unavailable after upgrading to op-reth v2.3.2
topIssues.author: Creamers158
topIssues.body:
After upgrading op-reth from v2.3.1 to v2.3.2 (while keeping the consensus-layer component at v1.19.1), the rollup node fails to initialize when using consensus-layer sync.

The same configuration works correctly with op-reth v2.3.1.

`t=2026-06-26T09:37:09+0000 lvl=error msg="Error initializing the rollup node" err="failed to init L2: failed to get L2 genesis blockhash: failed to determine L2BlockRef of height 0, could not get payload: pruned history unavailable" t=2026-06-26T09:37:09+0000 lvl=crit msg="Application failed" message="failed to setup: unable to create the rollup node: failed to init L2: failed to get L2 genesis blockhash: failed to determine L2BlockRef of height 0, could not get payload: pruned history unavailable"`

**Working (op-reth v2.3.1)**

```
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8545 \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"eth_getBlockByNumber","params":["0x0",false],"id":1}'
```

Returns the expected genesis block:
```
{
  "result": {
    "number": "0x0",
    "hash": "0x8ed4903b7f9c3f7bb7a09374d63ae9c9852cd9aab1784b433c41dbeb47b4dba2",
    ...
  }
}
```

**Failing (op-reth v2.3.2)**

**Running the same RPC request returns:**

```
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "error": {
    "code": 4444,
    "message": "pruned history unavailable"
  }
}
```

**Tracing the error in the source shows:**

ProviderError::BlockExpired
    ↓
EthApiError::PrunedHistoryUnavailable
    ↓
RPC error 4444 ("pruned history unavailable")

**Expected behavior**

When switching the execution layer to consensus sync mode, op-node should initialize successfully, as it does with op-reth v2.3.1.

During initialization, op-node resolves the L2 genesis block (height 0). eth_getBlockByNumber("0x0") is expected to return the L2 genesis block rather than 4444: pruned history unavailable, allowing consensus sync to start.

topIssues.title: fix: cantina #30 portal misses chain-ID check for non-super game roots
topIssues.author: stevennevins
topIssues.body:
OptimismPortal2.proveWithdrawalTransaction binds super-game roots to the portal's L2 chain ID by calling rootClaimByChainId(systemConfig.l2ChainId()). It does not do the same for non-super dispute games. For those games, it reads rootClaim() directly.

That skips a check that already exists on single-chain games. FaultDisputeGame.rootClaimByChainId reverts with UnknownChainId when the requested chain ID does not match the game's immutable l2ChainId(). Since the portal does not call that function for non-super games, it never independently confirms that the game root belongs to the chain configured in this portal's SystemConfig.

AnchorStateRegistry.isGameClaimValid does not close this gap. It checks that the game is registered, proper, respected, finalized and resolved in favor of the defender. It does not check that the game was created for this portal's L2 chain ID.

This is mainly a missing fail-closed check. In a normal deployment, OPCM and the standard validation process should put the correct L2 chain ID into the non-super game implementation arguments. An unprivileged user cannot normally choose that value. The likelihood of a potential issue, though, is quite low as this risky state requires a privileged factory registration, migration or owner-controlled upgrade that leaves this portal respecting a non-super game type configured for the wrong chain. Once that bad configuration exists, any proposer can create a game for the wrong chain. They can then prove a withdrawal against an output root from that other chain, wait for the game to resolve, and finalize through this portal. The portal therefore relies on deployment-time correctness for a consensus-critical value that the game interface can verify at runtime.

Recommendation:
Confirm the chainid matches the game.l2ChainId()

topIssues.title: [PCD Milestone 1.5] Add `deploy(FullConfig)` to L2ContractsManager as the L2Genesis code path
topIssues.author: 0xiamflux
topIssues.body:
### Context

We want a `deploy(FullConfig)` function in `L2ContractsManager` that serves as the branch of the L2CM that runs during L2Genesis. The goal is for the majority of the initialization code currently in the genesis script to instead reuse the L2CM deploy "mode", rather than duplicating the logic in the script.

This is analogous to the `OPCM.deploy` code path. Here, `deploy(FullConfig)` becomes the entrypoint used during L2Genesis to set up and initialize the predeploys, producing the correct genesis allocations.

### Definition of Done

- [ ] `deploy(FullConfig)` exists in `L2ContractsManager` and acts as the L2Genesis branch of the L2CM.
- [ ] L2Genesis uses `deploy(FullConfig)` to produce the genesis allocations.
- [ ] The produced genesis allocations are correct.
- [ ] Regression tests pass.

topPRs.title: op-proposer: resolve respected game type automatically
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Updates op-proposer so the default dispute game type is resolved from the current AnchorStateRegistry respected game type.

The proposer can now use `--network` or `--system-config-address` to resolve SystemConfig, then reload the current DisputeGameFactory and AnchorStateRegistry on each proposal cycle so upgrades are picked up without restarting. Explicit numeric `--game-type` values still behave as before, and `--game-factory-address` remains supported for backwards compatibility.

Validated with:
- `mise exec -- go test ./op-proposer/...`
- `mise exec -- go test ./packages/contracts-bedrock/snapshots`
- `git diff --check`

topPRs.title: feat: permissionless fault games at initial deploy
topPRs.author: lumoswiz
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Lets a new chain launch with permissionless fault games (Cannon and Cannon-Kona) enabled from genesis, not just the permissioned game. The deploy script used to require the permissioned game type and seed a placeholder anchor root. It now accepts the permissionless types, takes the real anchor root and per-game prestates as deploy inputs, and OP Contracts Manager allows those games at initial deploy. Default permissioned deploys are unchanged.

**Tests**
  * New chains using Cannon or Cannon-Kona now deploy, with both games enabled, the expected bonds and per-game prestates, and the anchor state registry seeded from the input.
  * Permissioned deploys still succeed and do not need the new permissionless inputs.
  * Invalid inputs revert: a missing or placeholder anchor root, missing prestates, and permissionless games requested alongside super roots.

**Additional context**

Part of the predictive-chain-deployments work (#20903). This PR adds and consumes the new deploy inputs, but they are still placeholders here. A follow-up (#20912) populates them from real pipeline state, so for now op-deployer and interopgen keep deploying the permissioned game with the old placeholder anchor and behavior does not change.

**Metadata**
  * Fixes #20913

topPRs.title: ci: make CircleCI workflow routing declarative
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Separates the CircleCI routing **data** from the routing **logic**. Stacked on #21579.

A new `.circleci/routing.yml` holds the declarative data:
- `schedules` — schedule name → workflows
- `api_dispatch` — dispatch flag → workflows (including `main_dispatch` and `labeled_pr`, whose conditions stay in the script)
- `change_patterns` — `any`/`all` ERE patterns matched against changed files
- `passthrough_params` — params forwarded to continuation configs

`compute-workflow-conditions.sh` now holds only the conditions; `collect-params.sh` reads the change patterns from `routing.yml`; and `test-schedule-triggers.js` reads the schedule map directly instead of regex-parsing the routing script.

No routing behavior changes — the same `c-run_*` flags are enabled for every trigger/branch/schedule/dispatch case.

## Test plan
- `mise exec -- bash .circleci/scripts/test-decision-tree.sh` — 19/19 scenarios pass (now reads `routing.yml`)
- `mise exec -- shellcheck .circleci/scripts/*.sh`
- `mise exec -- bash .circleci/scripts/merge-configs.sh && mise exec -- bash .circleci/scripts/test-continuation-params.sh /tmp/merged-config.yml`
- `mise exec -- bun build .circleci/scripts/test-schedule-triggers.js --outfile=/tmp/x.js`
- offline run of `bun .circleci/scripts/test-schedule-triggers.js` (live API portion needs `CIRCLE_API_TOKEN`)

topPRs.title: docs: split deposit-flow into explanation + replay tutorial
topPRs.author: sbvegan
topPRs.body:
## What

Splits `op-stack/bridging/deposit-flow.mdx`, which was serving three Diátaxis modes at once, into the right kinds of pages:

- **Explanation (stays):** `op-stack/bridging/deposit-flow.mdx` keeps the L1/L2 deposit mechanism and DoS-prevention concepts, plus a short "Replaying failed deposits" section that links out to the new tutorial.
- **Tutorial (new):** `app-developers/tutorials/bridging/replay-failed-deposit.mdx` holds the hands-on replay walkthrough and the debugging steps, with prerequisites and cross-links back to the explanation.
- **Nav:** adds the new tutorial under App Developers → Tutorials → Bridging in `docs.json`.

The technical steps and `cast` commands were moved **verbatim** — this is a structural split, not a content rewrite.

## Why

From the Diátaxis structure audit (finding `56e1ff39`, severity **high**, adversarially verified): the page mixed conceptual explanation, a hands-on tutorial, and reference/debugging in one place, which dilutes all three. Under Diátaxis a page should serve one reader need.

## Reviewer checklist
- [ ] The explanation page reads cleanly without the walkthrough.
- [ ] The tutorial stands alone (prereqs → steps → debugging) and both cross-links resolve.
- [ ] The `docs.json` entry lands in the right group.
- [ ] `mintlify dev` renders both pages.
